summary30s: The United Nations was established on 24 October 1945 as successor to the League of Nations, founded by 51 nations (India signed on 30 October 1945).
The UN Security Council consists of 5 Permanent Members (P-5: US, Russia, UK, France, China) with Veto power and 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms.
UN restructuring debates focus on expanding the Security Council; India strongly advocates for a permanent seat based on population, democracy, economy, and peacekeeping contributions.
Key specialized agencies include the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA, 1957), World Health Organization (WHO), and United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
Economic governance is dominated by the World Bank, International Monetary Fund (IMF, weighted voting), and the World Trade Organization (WTO, established 1 January 1995).

coreConcepts.title: Evolution and Structure of the United Nations
coreConcepts.explanation: The United Nations was established on 24 October 1945 following the devastation of World War II, succeeding the failed League of Nations. The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945 by 50 nations (Poland signed later as the 51st original founder). India joined on 30 October 1945. Today, it has 193 member states. Principal organs: General Assembly (all members have one vote), Security Council (15 members), Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), Trusteeship Council (suspended 1994), International Court of Justice (The Hague), and the Secretariat headed by the Secretary-General (Antonio Guterres). Second UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjold famously remarked: 'The UN was not created to take humanity to heaven, but to save it from hell.'
coreConcepts.examTip: UN Day: 24 October 1945. India joined on 30 October 1945. General Assembly: 193 members, 1 vote each.

coreConcepts.title: Reform of the UN Security Council and the Veto
coreConcepts.explanation: The Security Council has 5 permanent members (P-5: USA, Russia, UK, France, China) and 10 non-permanent members elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms (ineligible for immediate re-election). The P-5 enjoy the 'Veto power': a negative vote cast by ANY single permanent member stalls and defeats a substantive resolution, regardless of majority support. The Council's composition reflects 1945 geopolitical realities, not contemporary multipolarity. In 1997, UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan proposed criteria for new permanent members: (1) A major economic power, (2) A major military power, (3) A substantial contributor to the UN budget, (4) A big nation in terms of population, (5) A nation that respects democracy and human rights, (6) A country that makes the Council more representative of global diversity.
coreConcepts.examTip: A non-permanent member cannot be re-elected immediately after its two-year term. Veto power belongs exclusively to the P-5.

coreConcepts.title: India's Claim to a Permanent Security Council Seat
coreConcepts.explanation: India is the foremost contender for a permanent seat in an expanded Security Council. Arguments supporting India: (1) India is the world's most populous nation, representing nearly one-fifth of humanity; (2) India is the world's largest functioning democracy; (3) India has participated in almost all UN Peacekeeping Operations, suffering the highest casualties; (4) India is among the world's fastest-growing major economic powers; (5) India has made regular and timely financial contributions to the UN. Objections raised by critics: strained relations with Pakistan, nuclear weapon capabilities outside the NPT, and questions about whether other developing nations (Brazil, South Africa) would also demand seats.
coreConcepts.examTip: G-4 Nations: India, Brazil, Germany, and Japan support each other's bids for permanent seats in the UN Security Council.

coreConcepts.title: Specialized Agencies and Global NGOs
coreConcepts.explanation: Specialized international agencies address non-military global challenges: (1) International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA): Established in 1957 following US President Eisenhower's 'Atoms for Peace' proposal, promotes peaceful nuclear energy and inspects civilian reactors; (2) World Trade Organization (WTO): Established on 1 January 1995 as the successor to GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade), regulating multilateral trade; (3) International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank: Established at Bretton Woods (1944); feature weighted voting where the US holds veto power (>16% voting share); (4) Non-Governmental Organizations: Amnesty International (global NGO campaigning for human rights and political prisoners) and Human Rights Watch (advocacy NGO monitoring global civil liberties).
coreConcepts.examTip: WTO was established on 1 January 1995 as successor to GATT. IAEA headquarters is in Vienna, Austria.

workedExamples.question:
Which of the following is NOT one of the criteria proposed by UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan in 1997 for choosing new permanent members of the UN Security Council?
(A) A major economic power
(B) A major military power
(C) A country possessing an officially declared nuclear arsenal
(D) A substantial contributor to the UN budget
workedExamples.explanation: Possessing nuclear weapons was NOT a criterion. The criteria proposed by Kofi Annan included: major economic power, major military power, substantial budget contributor, big population, respect for democracy/human rights, and geographic diversity.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Check Kofi Annan's 1997 criteria from NCERT Chapter 6.
Step 2: Nuclear capability is explicitly absent from the official criteria.
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Except-pattern question on UN reform criteria.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Check Kofi Annan's 1997 criteria from NCERT Chapter 6.
Step 2: Nuclear capability is explicitly absent from the official criteria.

workedExamples.question:
The World Trade Organization (WTO) was established on 1 January 1995 as the successor to which international trade arrangement?
(A) UNCTAD
(B) GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade)
(C) Bretton Woods Monetary Agreement
(D) OEEC
workedExamples.explanation: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an international organisation which sets the rules for global trade. It was set up on 1 January 1995 as the successor to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Identify predecessor of WTO: GATT, formed in 1948.
Step 2: Replaced by WTO on 1 January 1995 following the Uruguay Round of negotiations.

commonTraps.misconception: Believing non-permanent members of the Security Council have Veto power.
commonTraps.correctConcept: ONLY the five permanent members (US, Russia, UK, France, China) possess the Veto. Non-permanent members have only one vote and NO veto power.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Questions ask how many votes are required to pass a resolution in the UNSC.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: Veto belongs exclusively to the P-5.

commonTraps.misconception: Thinking the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is located at UN headquarters in New York.
commonTraps.correctConcept: The ICJ is the ONLY principal organ of the UN located outside New York; it is seated at the Peace Palace in THE HAGUE, Netherlands.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Students assume all UN principal organs are in New York.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: ICJ is located at The Hague (Netherlands).

practiceQuestions.question: On which date did India formally become a member of the United Nations?
practiceQuestions.explanation: India joined the UN on 30 October 1945, six days after the UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.

practiceQuestions.question: How many non-permanent members are elected to the UN Security Council, and for what term length?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Security Council has ten non-permanent members elected by the General Assembly for a two-year term.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following principal organs of the United Nations is situated in The Hague (Netherlands) rather than New York?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The International Court of Justice is based in The Hague, Netherlands.

practiceQuestions.question: In 1957, which international agency was established following US President Dwight Eisenhower's 'Atoms for Peace' proposal?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) was established in 1957 to promote peaceful nuclear energy and prevent military misuse.

practiceQuestions.question: Which international non-governmental organization campaigns globally for the protection of human rights and the release of political prisoners of conscience?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Amnesty International is an international NGO that campaigns for the protection of human rights all over the world.

practiceQuestions.question: Which group of four countries (G-4) mutually support each other's candidatures for permanent seats in the UN Security Council?

options.text: India, Russia, China, and South Africa
USA, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand

practiceQuestions.explanation: The G-4 nations—India, Brazil, Germany, and Japan—mutually support each other's bids for permanent seats in the Security Council.

practiceQuestions.question: Who was the second Secretary-General of the United Nations who remarked that 'The UN was not created to take humanity to heaven, but to save it from hell'?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Dag Hammarskjold, the second UN Secretary-General, made this famous observation.

practiceQuestions.question: How many total member states are currently represented in the United Nations General Assembly?
practiceQuestions.explanation: There are currently 193 member states in the United Nations.

practiceQuestions.question: In the International Monetary Fund (IMF), why does the United States hold an effective unilateral veto over major structural policy decisions?

options.text: Because the IMF charter gives the US President automatic veto
Because the US holds more than 16% of total voting power and major decisions require an 85% supermajority
Because the IMF headquarters is in New York
Because all IMF loans are disbursed solely in US cash dollars

practiceQuestions.explanation: The US has over 16% of voting power in the IMF. Since key decisions require an 85% majority, the US alone can veto any resolution.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The abolition of the Veto power of the five permanent members of the Security Council is practically impossible under the current UN Charter.
Reason (R): Any amendment to the UN Charter requires the concurrence of all five permanent members, meaning any P-5 state can veto an amendment aimed at abolishing its own veto.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Charter amendment requires ratification by all P-5 states. None will vote to strip themselves of the veto. Both are true and (R) explains (A).
